questions.prompt: Your gross pay is ${g}. How much Social Security (6.2%) is withheld?
Total FICA is 7.65% of wages. On a ${g} paycheck, how much FICA is withheld?
questions.explanation: 7.65% × ${g} = ${ANSWER} (6.2% Social Security + 1.45% Medicare).

questions.prompt: Using Fin City brackets (10% to $11,925; 12% to $48,475; 22% to $103,350), what is the tax on taxable income of ${T}?
questions.explanation: Apply each rate to the dollars in its bracket: tax(${T}) = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Your gross income is ${G} and you take the $15,000 standard deduction. What is your EFFECTIVE federal tax rate (%)? Round to 0.1.
questions.explanation: Tax on ${G} − $15,000 is computed by brackets, then divided by ${G}: {ANSWER:pct}. Much lower than the top bracket!

questions.prompt: Your taxable income rises from $48,000 to $49,000, crossing into the 22% bracket. What happens?
choices: The whole raise is taxed at 0%
questions.explanation: Progressive brackets apply higher rates only to the dollars inside each bracket. A raise never reduces take-home pay.

questions.prompt: Which form do you give your employer to set how much income tax is withheld?
questions.explanation: The W-4 tells your employer how much to withhold. The W-2 reports what you earned and what was withheld.

questions.prompt: Freelancers usually receive which form instead of a W-2?
questions.explanation: Independent contractors get a 1099, and nothing is withheld, so they must set aside tax themselves.

questions.prompt: Self-employed people pay both halves of FICA: 15.3%. On ${p} of freelance profit, how much self-employment tax is that?
questions.explanation: 15.3% × ${p} = ${ANSWER}. (Simplified, real rules adjust the base slightly.)

questions.prompt: In the 22% bracket, which saves more tax: a $1,000 deduction or a $1,000 credit?
questions.explanation: A deduction lowers taxable income (saving 22% × $1,000 = $220). A credit cuts tax dollar-for-dollar.

questions.prompt: Wages ${W}, withholding ${H}. Standard deduction $15,000. Refund (positive) or amount owed (negative)?
questions.explanation: Tax = brackets on ${W} − $15,000. Withheld − tax = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Itemized deductions total $11,000. The standard deduction is $15,000. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Take whichever is larger. $15,000 > $11,000, so standard wins.

questions.prompt: A traditional 401(k)-style contribution of $3,000 for someone in the 12% bracket lowers this year's income tax by about…
questions.explanation: Pre-tax contributions reduce taxable income: 12% × $3,000 = $360.

questions.prompt: An annual salary of ${S} is paid every two weeks (26 paychecks). What is each gross paycheck?
You earn ${r}/hour and work 40 hours a week, 52 weeks a year. What is the annual salary equivalent?
questions.explanation: ${r} × 2,080 hours = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Overtime pays 1.5× after 40 hours. You earn ${r}/hr and work {h} hours this week. Gross pay?
Negotiating your first salary up by ${d}, with 3% raises every year, adds how much over 40 years? (Sum of a growing series: d × ((1.03)^40 − 1)/0.03)
questions.explanation: ${d} × ((1.03^40 − 1) / 0.03) = ${ANSWER}. Small raises early compound for a whole career.

questions.prompt: In salary negotiation, what is a BATNA?
choices: Your best alternative if talks fail
The first offer on the table
questions.explanation: Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement, knowing it tells you when to walk away.

questions.prompt: A job pays $60,000; another pays $56,000 but includes a 6% retirement match you'd use fully and $3,000/yr better health coverage. Which offers more total compensation?
choices: Benefits can’t be compared to pay
questions.explanation: $56,000 + 6% match ($3,360) + $3,000 benefits ≈ $62,360 > $60,000. Compare total compensation, not just salary.

questions.prompt: You have {n} vested options with a ${k} strike. Shares trade at ${p}. Intrinsic value (before tax)?
A 4-year vesting schedule with a 1-year cliff means if you leave after 10 months you get…
questions.explanation: Nothing vests until the 1-year cliff. Leaving at 10 months forfeits the grant.

questions.prompt: Which is the strongest protection if your password leaks?
choices: Adding “!” to the end of it
Keeping it on a sticky note
questions.explanation: 2FA requires a second proof (app code or key), so a stolen password alone isn't enough.

questions.prompt: What does a credit freeze do?
choices: Blocks new credit in your name
questions.explanation: A freeze blocks lenders from pulling your report, preventing thieves from opening accounts. It's free and you can lift it when needed.

questions.prompt: A 'job' offers $900/week to deposit checks and wire 80% to others. This is…
questions.explanation: The checks bounce days later; you owe the bank everything you wired, and may be helping launder money.

questions.prompt: Which details are most valuable to identity thieves? (Select all)
questions.explanation: SSN, birthdate and passwords let thieves open accounts or take over yours.

questions.prompt: You notice an unfamiliar $1 charge on your card. Why does it matter?
choices: Thieves test stolen cards with tiny charges
It doesn’t: it’s only $1, so let it go
It’s interest the card charges monthly
It’s a refund that hasn’t posted yet
questions.explanation: Small test charges often come before large fraud. Report it and get a new card.

questions.prompt: Which website address is most likely the real Fin City Bank?
questions.explanation: The real domain is the part right before the first single slash. Look-alikes add words or change the ending.

questions.prompt: Your wage rises {w}% this year while inflation is {i}%. What is your approximate REAL wage change (%)?
questions.explanation: (1 + {w}%)/(1 + {i}%) − 1 ≈ {ANSWER:pct}. If it's negative, your buying power fell even though your paycheck grew.

questions.prompt: A certificate program costs ${c} and raises your pay by ${r}/year. How many years to break even (ignoring interest)?
questions.explanation: ${c} ÷ ${r} per year = {ANSWER} years. Education is an investment in human capital.

questions.prompt: Why do software engineers in a tech hub often earn more than the national average?
choices: High demand, limited supply of skills
A state law requires higher pay
Rents are high, and that’s the only reason
They work fewer hours than average
questions.explanation: Wages reflect supply and demand for skills (and local cost of living). Scarce, in-demand skills pay more.

questions.prompt: A ${s}/month subscription you rarely use costs how much over 3 years?
questions.explanation: ${s} × 36 months = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Net pay is ${n}/month. Rent ${r}, food ${f}, transport ${t}. What % of net pay is left?
Rent should be no more than about 30% of gross income (a common guideline). Gross pay is $4,500/month. Which rent fits?
Rideshare driving pays ${g}/hour gross, but costs ${c}/hour in fuel and wear. You also set aside 15.3% of net profit for self-employment tax. True hourly earnings?
questions.explanation: (${g} − ${c}) × (1 − 0.153) = ${ANSWER}/hour. Gig work's real pay is lower than the headline.

questions.prompt: Taxable income is ${T}. What is the marginal rate (%)? (10% to 11,925; 12% to 48,475; 22% to 103,350; 24% to 197,300)
questions.explanation: The marginal rate is the rate on your last dollar of taxable income: {ANSWER:pct} for ${T}.

questions.prompt: Gross pay minus taxes and deductions equals…
questions.explanation: Net pay is your take-home pay.

questions.prompt: Sales tax is called 'regressive' because…
choices: Lower incomes pay a bigger share
It rises as your income rises
questions.explanation: Everyone pays the same rate on purchases, but lower earners spend a bigger share of income, so it takes a bigger bite.

questions.prompt: Federal withholding per biweekly paycheck is ${f}. Over 26 paychecks, total withheld?
A $2,000 signing bonus vs. a $2,000 higher salary: which is worth more over time?
choices: The salary: it repeats and raises build on it
The bonus: you get it all up front
questions.explanation: A bonus is paid once. A salary increase repeats and compounds with raises.

questions.prompt: Your employer matches 50% of contributions up to 6% of pay. You earn ${S} and contribute 6%. How much does the employer add per year?
questions.explanation: 6% × ${S} × 50% = ${ANSWER}. That's an instant 50% return on your contribution.

questions.prompt: If your employer matches up to 6% and you contribute only 2%, you are…
choices: Leaving free money on the table
Paying more tax on the match
questions.explanation: Contribute at least enough to get the full match, it's part of your pay.

questions.prompt: An 'investment' promises guaranteed 30% monthly returns and pays early investors from new investors' money. This is a…
questions.explanation: Paying old investors with new investors' money collapses when new money slows. Guaranteed high returns are the red flag.

questions.prompt: What does 'phishing' mean?
choices: A website with a secure padlock
questions.explanation: Phishing uses fake emails, texts or sites that look real to steal passwords and money.

questions.prompt: The unemployment rate rises during a recession. What usually happens to wage growth?
choices: It slows: more people compete for jobs
It speeds up as companies compete
It doesn’t change during a recession
questions.explanation: More job seekers relative to openings reduces workers' bargaining power.

questions.prompt: Offer A: ${a} salary in a city where rent is ${ra}/month. Offer B: ${b} salary where rent is ${rb}/month. Which leaves more per year after rent? Enter the DIFFERENCE (A − B).
questions.explanation: (${a} − 12×${ra}) − (${b} − 12×${rb}) = ${ANSWER}. Cost of living matters (taxes would shrink the gap further).

questions.prompt: Lifestyle creep means…
questions.explanation: If spending grows with every raise, savings never improve. Bank part of each raise first.

questions.prompt: You get a ${r}/month raise and commit to saving half of it at 6% APR (monthly). How much after 5 years?
questions.explanation: Saving ${r} ÷ 2 per month for 60 months at 0.5%/month ≈ ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Roth vs. traditional: which is generally better if you expect to be in a HIGHER bracket in retirement?
choices: Roth: pay tax now at the lower rate
questions.explanation: Roth contributions are taxed now; withdrawals later are tax-free. That wins if your future rate is higher.

questions.prompt: A ${b} raise is offered as a {p}% raise on your ${s} salary or a flat ${b}. What is the {p}% raise in dollars?
questions.explanation: {p}% × ${s} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Your data was in a breach. Best order of actions?
choices: Ignore it unless money goes missing
Post about it publicly to warn friends
questions.explanation: Secure your email first (it resets everything else), add 2FA, freeze credit, and watch for fraud.

questions.prompt: Automation replaces some routine tasks. Which response best protects your earning power?
choices: Avoid training so your role stays the same
Rely on one employer for your whole career
Stop working until the changes settle
questions.explanation: Skills that work alongside technology (analysis, design, communication) stay in demand.

questions.prompt: Fin City's city tax is 3% of gross wages. On annual wages of ${W}, how much city tax?
Which counts as total compensation?
questions.explanation: Compare jobs on total compensation, not just salary.
